analysis.subject: physics
analysis.pageCoverage: Page covers the structure of the International System of Units, including seven defining constants, 7 base units, 22 derived units with special names, Twenty-four prefixes, writing conventions, treaty history and definitions of quantity, unit and value with an example.

overview.headline: How the SI defines and organizes measurement units

keyPoints.point: The SI rests on seven defining constants including the Planck constant and the speed of light in vacuum.
keyPoints.quote: The SI rests on a foundation of seven (7) defining constants

keyPoints.point: The SI contains 7 base units that define 22 derived units with special names and symbols.
keyPoints.quote: The SI is made up of 7 base units that define the 22 derived units with special names and symbols

keyPoints.point: The base units and derived units with special names form a core set of twenty-nine SI units.
keyPoints.quote: Together the base units and derived units with special names (twenty-nine units) form the core set of SI units.

keyPoints.point: The value of a physical quantity is expressed as the product of a number and a unit, such as a height of 169 m.
keyPoints.quote: the value of the height hW of the Washington Monument is hW = 169 m

keyPoints.point: Twenty-four prefixes ranging from 10^30 to 10^−30 modify unit magnitude.
keyPoints.quote: Twenty-four prefixes ranging from 10^30 to 10^−30, are currently recognized for use.

keyTerms.gloss: SI base unit for amount of substance
SI base unit for Length measurement
quantity used in mathematical equations of science
keyTerms.quote: A physical quantity is a quantity that can be used in the mathematical equations of science and technology.

keyTerms.gloss: particular physical quantity adopted by convention to express value
keyTerms.quote: A unit is a particular physical quantity, defined and adopted by convention

keyTerms.gloss: quantitative expression of a physical quantity as product of number and unit
keyTerms.quote: The value of a physical quantity is the quantitative expression of a particular physical quantity as the product of a number and a unit

componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Sorting helps students distinguish base units from derived units and see how the SI builds complexity from a small core set.
componentPlan.focusQuote: Together the base units and derived units with special names (twenty-nine units) form the core set of SI units.

componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Quiz cards reinforce checkable facts such as prefix limits and the definition of value as number times unit for accurate measurement literacy.
componentPlan.focusQuote: Twenty-four prefixes ranging from 10^30 to 10^−30, are currently recognized for use.
